roadmap_item: area I: the `max` combination form (and `or`, the other form of grn.ACTIVATOR_RULES never held against measured RNA) on 7d's population, registered
question: For genes the compiled programs drive through two or more elements, does a reader-gated run under the independent-binding combination form (grn `or`: A = 1 - prod(1 - t_i)), at one magnitude scale fitted on training genes and applied unchanged to held-out genes, track measured RNA across the thirteen reader cell types better than a no-rule baseline on the held-out genes? And is `max` testable on this endpoint at all?

form_sources.max: runtime/grn.py combine_activators 'max': A = max over the gene's activating rules of s_i*H(x_i), a held rule counted at strength 0 (so A = 0 with every activator held). One of the four rules lane-combine compared on 2026-09-28 (grn.ACTIVATOR_RULES), selectable for one run with NetworkRuntime(activator_combination='max'). Inhibitors multiply, R = prod (1 - s_j*H(x_j)), as under the mean. It is the lower end of lane-strengthform's additive_envelope (lane-envelope's identity checks, df02887)
form_sources.or: runtime/grn.py combine_activators 'or': A = 1 - prod over the gene's activating rules of (1 - s_i*H(x_i)), independent binding of any one activator sufficing; a held rule is counted at strength 0 and so drops out of the product. One of the four rules lane-combine compared on 2026-09-28 (grn.ACTIVATOR_RULES; grn.COMBINATION_TEST, 'or max <= P <= S1+S2'), selectable for one run with NetworkRuntime(activator_combination='or'). Inhibitors multiply, as under the mean

conventions: combine2's, unchanged (FIT['principle'] and FIT['mean']): every element at its intact state x = bridge.INTACT, so H(x) = bridge.H_INTACT = 0.5; the strongest activating element at bridge.DECLARED_STRENGTH (s = 1); an inhibitor's s_j*h = e_j/(q + e_j) at the form's own element-driven share q; the bridge's Hill assumptions (K = 1, n = 2, h = 0.5). No number is added and no parameter is tuned to any measured RNA value

premise.as_handed_to_this_lane: lane-envelope's conclusion, carried in this lane's brief: on 7d's design the runtime mean is linear under the reader's hold, and so is any sum below its cap, so no additive rule can separate from the mean at 7d's size; only a rule non-linear under the hold -- `max`, `or` -- or the capped root could be tested on this endpoint
premise.the_linear_half_holds: VERIFIED here from the same algebra, not taken on trust. Module.active_rules returns a held rule as a strength-0 copy and keeps it, and the bridge's removal is a clamp of the element at 0 with the rule kept (combine2.STRUCTURE['mean_is_linear_under_the_hold']). Under both, the mean's drive A = (1/n) sum t_i is linear in the element terms, so closing element i lowers transcription by d_i of T whatever the other elements do, and a capped sum below its cap is the same function of the open set up to the scale the fit absorbs. Hence an additive rule's centred prediction IS the mean's on every gene both fit, which is what lane-capsumrna measured (largest difference 6.66e-16 log2 over 2,288 genes) rather than argued
premise.the_conclusion_is_wrong_about_max: non-linearity under the hold is NECESSARY for a form to separate from the mean here and NOT SUFFICIENT, because a form must first reproduce every element's own removal observation (combine2.FIT['principle']). Under `max`, A = max t_i, so removing a non-maximal activator leaves A unchanged: d_i = Z*(A_full - A_without_i) = 0 for every activator but the strongest. 7d's POPULATION (b) requires every rule's observation to be readable and not exactly 1, so every activating element has d_i > 0, and `max` therefore has NO FIT on any gene with two or more activating elements -- not a worse fit, no fit. grn.COMBINATION_TEST already registered the same impossibility from a different measurement ('crispri_training_two_decreases': 'impossible under max (removing a non-maximal activator changes nothing)'). On a gene with exactly ONE activating element (and one or more inhibitors, which is how such a gene is in 7d's multi-element population) `max` reduces to that single term and is the mean element for element: the same q, the same fitted strengths, the same V, the same prediction in every reader cell. grn says as much in ACTIVATOR_RULES' own comment, 'all four agree when a gene has one activator'. So on 7d's population `max` either has no fit or gives the runtime mean's prediction exactly, and the count of genes where its prediction differs from the mean's is 0 BEFORE any RNA value is read
premise.or_is_the_form_the_premise_was_reaching_: `or` is non-linear under the hold and every activator's removal lowers it, so it can reproduce k drops at once: A = 1 - P with P = prod(1 - t_i), and removing i gives A = 1 - P/(1 - t_i), so d_i = Z*P*t_i/(1 - t_i) > 0 for every activator. FIT['or'] solves it in closed form, the solution is unique at combine2's conventions, and its centred prediction is not the mean's wherever the gene has two or more activating elements. It is the arm this registration judges
premise.what_this_lane_does_not_claim: that no form could test this endpoint. It establishes that an additive form cannot (three lanes today) and that `max` cannot be fitted at all on this population, and it tests `or`. A form outside grn.ACTIVATOR_RULES, a different population, or a fresh measurement are each untouched by any of it

fit.principle: the bridge's: the run reproduces each element's own removal observation RHO_i = 2**(log2 fold change on deletion) exactly at the state where every element of the gene is present (S5, 'direction and fold ... are the input'), and the gene's intact transcription is its rate T (measured, else the borrowed median; no fold prediction depends on T)
fit.max: d_i = 1 - RHO_i (activating), e_j = RHO_j - 1 (inhibiting). With two or more activating elements there is no fit (max_needs_one_activating_element): A = max t_i, so removing any activator but the strongest leaves A, and hence the level, unchanged, while every activating element of 7d's population has an observed drop. With exactly one activating element, A = t_1 with it open and 0 with it held, so d_1 = Z*H at s_1 = 1: Z = d_1/H, q = Z*H = d_1, b = T(1 - q), s_j*h = e_j/(q + e_j), V = T*Z/R0 -- combine2.fit('mean')'s numbers for n = 1, element for element. Level relative to T with the open set O: (1 - q) + Z*max(t_i over open activators, else 0) * prod over closed inhibitors (1 + e_j/q), which for one activator is the mean's (1 - q) + [d_1 if open] * that product
fit.or: d_i = 1 - RHO_i (activating), e_j = RHO_j - 1 (inhibiting), top = max d_i. Writing u_i = t_i/(1 - t_i) and P = prod(1 - t_i), the removal of activator i gives d_i = Z*P*u_i, so u_i is proportional to d_i; the DECLARED_STRENGTH convention puts the strongest activator at s = 1, i.e. t_top = H = 0.5 and u_top = H/(1 - H) = 1, which fixes the constant: u_i = d_i/top, t_i = d_i/(top + d_i), P = prod top/(top + d_i), Z = top/P and the element-driven share q = Z*(1 - P) = Z - top. Every activator's s_i = t_i/H = 2*d_i/(top + d_i) is in (0, 1] by construction, so only q < 1 and the inhibitors can refuse a gene. b = T(1 - q), s_j*h = e_j/(q + e_j), V = T*Z/R0 with R0 = prod(1 - s_j*h). Level relative to T with the open set O: (1 - q) + Z*(1 - prod over open activators of (1 - t_i)) * prod over closed inhibitors (1 + e_j/q)
fit.the_or_root_is_unique: u_i proportional to d_i is forced by the k removal equations, and the one free constant is fixed by the DECLARED_STRENGTH convention, whose 'strongest' is unambiguous because t_i = d_i/(top + d_i) is increasing in d_i, so argmax s = argmax d. There is no second root, and lane-rootpick's registered root convention (both roots exist -> the uncapped; the capped root alone -> the gene is UNKNOWN and leaves the population) is therefore not triggered by either form here: it is cited and applied vacuously. Under `max` the question does not arise either -- a gene with two or more activating elements has no root at all
fit.where_the_forms_can_differ: MEASURED, not assumed, and it is what the census counts: every form here is fitted to the same single-removal observations, so on any state in which AT MOST ONE of a gene's activating elements is closed, every form gives the same level by construction. A form can only separate from the mean in a cell where TWO OR MORE of the gene's activating elements are closed at once. So a gene whose thirteen reader cells never close two of its activating elements together has `or`'s prediction equal to the mean's in all thirteen, however non-linear the form is, and the census counts it as not differing. The census question is therefore a question about the reader's open/closed pattern as much as about the form, and it is answered on the thirteen actual reader cells and not on hypothetical states
fit.q_rises_with_the_product: q_or = top*(prod(1 + d_i/top) - 1) >= sum d_i = q_mean, with equality only at one activating element: `or` saturates, so a single removal moves a nearly-saturated drive very little and the dynamic range Z needed to reproduce the measured drop is larger. Genes with several strong activating elements therefore leave no positive basal rate under `or` (basal_not_positive) and are not run, exactly as 7d's own populations exclude genes whose summed drops exceed T. The opposite also follows: q_or above q_mean makes an inhibitor's fitted s_j = 2*e_j/(q + e_j) SMALLER, so `or` admits inhibitors the mean refuses, and its population is not a subset of 7d's
fit.runnable: a gene is runnable under a form when the fit gives b > 0 (q < 1) and every fitted s in (0, 1] (bridge.STRENGTH_TOLERANCE above 1 allowed), 7d's FIT['runnable'] unchanged; otherwise it is reported by reason and not run

structure.what_is_assumed: that a gene's k observations were taken at one state. Under the reader selection a gene's rules come from k different argmax tracks; the joint fit treats them as one intact state, and each reader cell's run transports them there, as M2b transported one rule's m
structure.inhibitor_only: a gene with no activating rule has A = 1 under every activator form, so the forms cannot differ on it and its q is fixed by no observation; it is not run
structure.network: no compiled rule's source is a gene (runrules census): one independent system per gene

population: for each form F, every gene G such that, over all 24 compiled programs (data/knowledge/compiled, pinned by sha256) gated with compile.gate_program(selection='reader_cells'): (a) two or more activates/inhibits rule lines target G, all in one program, all of predicted evidence, each acting through its own element; (b) every rule's removal observation is readable (bridge.observation_of) and none is exactly 1; (c) at least one rule is activating; (d) the joint fit under F is runnable (FIT['runnable']); (e) the gated prediction under F is not the same in all thirteen reader cells (its range exceeds INFORMATIVE_LOG2 in log2); (f) G's symbol names exactly one gene_id in data/cache/gencode_genes.tsv and that gene_id is on exactly one row of every one of the thirteen quantification tables. (a)-(e) are predictor-side: no measured value enters them. Each G contributes its thirteen (G, cell) pairs. No filter on expression
population_note: 7d's POPULATION above is carried verbatim and its clause (d), 'the joint fit under F is runnable', is read with F = `or` and FIT['or']; clause (e)'s informativeness and clause (f)'s symbol and row checks are unchanged. The population is therefore NOT 7d's gene set: `or`'s q exceeds the mean's, so genes whose summed drops saturate it leave no positive basal rate and drop out, while `or` admits inhibitors the mean refuses and keeps genes 7d's mean does not run (FIT['q_rises_with_the_product']). The census counts the overlap, and the head-to-head is on the genes the compared forms both run
prior_exposure: STATED PLAINLY, AND NOT A CAVEAT ADDED AFTERWARDS. This measurement is not fresh for this project. The same ENCODE polyA plus RNA-seq of the same thirteen reader biosamples, under the same log2(TPM+1) endpoint and the same no-rule baseline, has already been read by: item 7 (M2b, lane-readercompile, data/results/readergate_result.json) including its post-hoc information term; item 7d (M2c, lane-combine2) for the runtime's mean and promoter competition; item 7h (M2f, lane-multrna) for the multiplicative composition; item M2h (lane-magcal, ac5580b) for all three of those forms at one fitted magnitude scale on a held-out split; and today's capped-sum census (lane-capsumrna) and additive-envelope census (lane-envelope), both of which reached NOT_TESTABLE without opening an RNA table. The genes this lane reads are largely the same genes, and the choice to try another combination form at all was made BECAUSE the earlier readings came out worse than no rule uncalibrated and because M2h's calibrated multiplicative arm came out better. The held-out split limits that exposure and does not eliminate it: the split is fixed by this registration before any held-out number is read and no held-out gene enters any fit, but those genes' RNA values were in the earlier readings' populations, the endpoint and baseline were chosen with those readings in hand, and nothing here is a blind prediction of an unseen measurement. Any reading from this lane therefore holds as a statement about THIS measurement and is not independent confirmation of it; a magnitude read here is a hypothesis for a fresh measurement, not a result on one
prior_exposure_clause: carried with every reading: this RNA is not a fresh measurement. The same ENCODE polyA plus RNA-seq of the same thirteen reader biosamples under the same endpoint was read by items 7, 7d and 7h and by today's capped-sum census, and the P and D calibrated here are 7d's and 7h's committed rows; the held-out split limits that exposure and does not eliminate it, so a reading here is a statement about this measurement and a hypothesis for a fresh one, not independent confirmation
split: held out when int(sha256(symbol as UTF-8).hexdigest()[:8], 16) is odd, training when even (scripts/saturable_gate.is_held_out, the convention lane-saturable registered today, taken unchanged); the split is on the gene SYMBOL, so a gene falls the same side in every form, is fixed by this registration before any held-out number is read, and depends on no measured value. A gene is wholly on one side with all thirteen of its pairs: no cell of a held-out gene enters any fit

predictions.form: s_F(G, X) = log2(L_F(G, X)), L_F(G, X) the level the runtime gives G in reader cell X under F = `or` (NetworkRuntime(..., activator_combination='or'), the fitted rules acting through their elements, the reader blocks in force, every element clamped present so that only the reader holds a rule). P_F(G, X) = s_F(G, X) - mean over the thirteen cells of s_F(G, X'), 7d's centring unchanged
predictions.scaled_form: a*P_F(G, X), one scale a per form for the whole population, fitted on the TRAINING genes' pairs alone and applied unchanged to the held-out genes (magcal.FIT, taken unchanged)
predictions.no_rule_baseline: P(G, X) = 0: G's level in X equals its mean over the thirteen reader cells

fit_scale: a_F is the one scale that minimises the squared error over the TRAINING pairs of form F, in closed form: a_F = (sum over training pairs of D*P_F) / (sum over training pairs of P_F^2); it is undefined, and the form is NOT_FITTABLE, when the denominator is 0. Equivalently it is the scale that maximises Delta MSE on the training pairs. It is fitted on training pairs only; no held-out value enters it. a_F = 1 is the uncalibrated form, which is what 7d and 7h read
metric: Delta MSE(F, a) = mean over the pairs of D^2 - mean of (D - a*P_F)^2 = mean of (2a*D*P_F - a^2*P_F^2) (combine2.METRIC with the calibrated prediction in place of P), positive when the scaled form's squared error is below the no-rule baseline's. The registered endpoint is this quantity on the HELD-OUT pairs at a = a_F, with a_F fitted on the training pairs. Reported beside it, deciding nothing: the same quantity on the held-out pairs at a = 1 (the uncalibrated form on the held-out genes) and on the training pairs at a = a_F
family: the family corrected over is four: 7d's runtime mean, 7d's promoter-competition form, 7h's multiplicative composition and this lane's arm. The same RNA, the same endpoint, the same no-rule baseline and the same held-out split, so a fourth arm changes the correction; 95%/4 gives 98.75% two-sided, percentiles 0.625 and 99.375. M2h's three arms keep their registered 98.33% intervals and are not recomputed here

bootstrap.unit: gene: genes are resampled with replacement and carry all thirteen of their pairs
bootstrap.interval: the 98.75% percentile interval (Bonferroni over the family of four, FAMILY) of the held-out Delta MSE at the fitted scale, the scale held fixed; and the 98.75% percentile interval of the scale itself over TRAINING gene resamples, refitted in each. magcal's `_gene_terms` and `_sums` build the resampling statistic unchanged; only the percentile pair is this registration's, because magcal's bootstrap_delta and bootstrap_scale read magcal's own FORM_INTERVAL and lane-magcal's files are not edited by this lane. tests/test_maxform.py checks that this lane's bootstrap, run at magcal.FORM_INTERVAL, reproduces magcal.bootstrap_delta and magcal.bootstrap_scale exactly

control: a within-gene cell permutation, this lane's own and NOT 7d's or 7h's shuffled-reader control (see CARRIED['note']): for each permutation, each gene's thirteen P values are permuted among its own thirteen cells by an independent draw of the seeded generator, every gene keeping its own prediction values, its own range and its own side of the split, and every pair keeping its own D. Only the tie between a prediction and the cell it was made for is broken. The scale is REFITTED on the permuted training pairs and the permuted held-out Delta MSE is computed, so the control asks exactly what the registered endpoint asks of a form whose magnitudes survive and whose cell alignment does not. PERMUTATIONS['count'] permutations at PERMUTATIONS['seed']; control p = (1 + permutations with held-out Delta MSE >= observed) / (1 + count)
control_note: magcal's control, taken unchanged: a WITHIN-GENE cell permutation, which asks whether the rules' cell-to-cell pattern carries anything beyond a gene-level offset, the question the supervisor's audit of M2h called the right one. control p = (1 + permutations with held-out Delta MSE >= observed) / (1 + PERMUTATIONS['count']), so with 1,000 permutations the smallest p it can report is 0.000999: a p of 0.000999 is the FLOOR of the control and not a smaller number
harness: for every gene run under the form: (1) in each of the thirteen reader cells the gated run's level equals T times the form's closed form for that cell's open set; (2) the same fitted program with its rules ungated, every element present, then each element clamped absent in turn, reproduces that element's RHO. Each within CLOSED_FORM_TOLERANCE in log2 (7d's HARNESS, unchanged). Any miss stops the run before the RNA is opened (HARNESS_DEFECT). Beside it, the census's own checks: max_identity_checks must return 0.0 on all three claims, and the recomputed 7d and 7h census counts must equal the committed ones
not_vacuous: a scale fitted to near 0 makes the calibrated prediction near-identical to the no-rule baseline, so its held-out Delta MSE comes out near 0 and the interval straddles 0. A dead scale can therefore MANUFACTURE A STRADDLE but it cannot manufacture a win: a held-out interval wholly above 0 requires the scaled prediction to lower the squared error on genes that entered no fit, which a prediction shrunk to nothing cannot do. 'better' is the one reading the vacuity trap cannot fake, which is why the held-out interval decides and the scale interval is what tells a dead-scale straddle (CALIBRATION_REMOVES, a negative) from a live-scale straddle (INCONCLUSIVE)

scale_clauses.fitted: fitted scale {a} [{ci} {alo}, {ahi}], one number for the whole form, fitted on {tg} training genes ({tn} gene-cell pairs) and applied unchanged to the held-out genes; the uncalibrated size 7d and 7h read is 1
scale_clauses.negative: the rules point the wrong way on average: the scale that best fits the training genes is negative (scale {a} [{ci} {alo}, {ahi}], fitted on {tg} training genes), so the measured level moves against the compiled prediction
scale_clauses.not_fittable: no scale is defined: the training pairs carry no prediction variance (sum of P^2 is 0)

outcomes.NOT_TESTABLE: {form}: not testable at the registered size; {g} held-out genes, fewer than the registered {min}; no comparison was read ({scale})
outcomes.BETTER: {form}: better; on genes held out of the fit, the reader-gated run scaled by the one factor fitted on the training genes lowered the squared error of measured log2(TPM+1) across the thirteen reader cell types below the no-rule baseline's, so it is closer to measured RNA than the no-rule baseline (held-out Delta MSE {d} [{ci} {lo}, {hi}] over {n} gene-cell pairs, {g} genes; control p = {p}; {scale})
outcomes.WORSE: {form}: worse; on genes held out of the fit, the reader-gated run scaled by the one factor fitted on the training genes raised the squared error of measured log2(TPM+1) across the thirteen reader cell types above the no-rule baseline's, so it is further from measured RNA than the no-rule baseline even at its best single magnitude (held-out Delta MSE {d} [{ci} {lo}, {hi}] over {n} gene-cell pairs, {g} genes; control p = {p}; {scale})
outcomes.CALIBRATION_REMOVES: {form}: calibration removes the rules: no magnitude of the compiled rules improves on no rule; the held-out interval straddles 0 and the training-set scale interval includes 0, so the calibration is not distinguishable from switching the compiled rules off (held-out Delta MSE {d} [{ci} {lo}, {hi}] over {n} gene-cell pairs, {g} genes; control p = {p}; {scale}). This is a negative result and is not 'no difference detected'
outcomes.INCONCLUSIVE: {form}: inconclusive; the held-out interval straddles 0 while the training-set scale interval excludes 0, so a magnitude is estimated and this measurement does not resolve whether the scaled run is closer to or further from measured RNA than the no-rule baseline (held-out Delta MSE {d} [{ci} {lo}, {hi}] over {n} gene-cell pairs, {g} genes; control p = {p}; {scale})
outcomes.HARNESS_DEFECT: stopped before anything was split, fitted or read: the committed genes tables did not reproduce their committed readings' numbers ({what})

decision: 1. The census is counted first and reads no RNA. Per form, fewer than MIN_GENES genes whose prediction differs from the runtime mean's (informative, symbol on exactly one gene_id) is NOT_TESTABLE and the census is that form's result: no registration, no RNA table opened (DECISION_BEFORE_THE_CENSUS). 2. If any gene misses the HARNESS, the run stops before the RNA is opened (HARNESS_DEFECT). 3. The split is applied (SPLIT). 4. One scale is fitted on the TRAINING pairs alone and bootstrapped on training genes. 5. ONLY THEN is the held-out Delta MSE computed at that scale, with its 98.75% interval and the within-gene cell permutation control, and magcal's four-way table (WHICH_GOVERNS, magcal.decide) applied as written: held-out interval wholly above 0 -> BETTER, wholly below -> WORSE, straddling 0 with the scale interval also straddling 0 -> CALIBRATION_REMOVES, straddling 0 with the scale interval excluding 0 -> INCONCLUSIVE. 6. The uncalibrated head-to-heads against the runtime mean and the multiplicative form, over the genes both forms run, are reported beside it as DESCRIPTIVE and decide nothing, because this lane's registered endpoint is the calibrated held-out one. 7. The reading is magcal's sentence for the outcome with the prior-exposure clause attached, always
decision_before_the_census: fixed before the census was counted, from PREMISE: per form, the genes whose fit gives a prediction differing from the runtime mean's by more than CLOSED_FORM_TOLERANCE in any reader cell, informative and with a symbol on exactly one gene_id, are the population a registration could test. Fewer than MIN_GENES of them is NOT_TESTABLE for that form (7d's DECISION 2, carried unchanged): no registration is written for it, no RNA table is opened for it, and the census is the result. At or above MIN_GENES the form is registered and run once. If BOTH forms are NOT_TESTABLE, the finding is that this endpoint separates no form tried so far -- additive (three lanes today), strongest-element, or independent-binding -- from the runtime mean on 7d's population, which is itself the result
inconclusive: 'inconclusive' is magcal's INCONCLUSIVE and means exactly this: the held-out Delta MSE interval includes 0 while the fitted scale's interval excludes it, so the form carries a magnitude this measurement can see but the held-out gain at that magnitude is not separated from zero at 98.75%. It is not evidence that the form tracks the RNA and not evidence that it does not. It is distinct from CALIBRATION_REMOVES, where the scale interval includes 0 as well and the best scale this measurement supports may be no rule at all, and from NOT_TESTABLE, which is a size verdict reached before any RNA value is read
falsifier: the form's held-out reading does not beat the no-rule baseline at the registered interval (its 98.75% held-out Delta MSE interval includes 0 or lies below it): run under this form at one fitted magnitude, the compiled rules of multi-element genes do not make a run track measured RNA across the reader's cell types in this population better than no rule. The narrower claim that the rules' CELL-TO-CELL pattern carries it, rather than a gene-level offset, is falsified when the within-gene permutation control is not beaten (control p > CONTROL_ALPHA). The claim that the form carries a magnitude at all is falsified when the fitted scale's interval includes 0. A negative fitted scale whose interval lies wholly below 0 falsifies the form's DIRECTION on this population (magcal.scale_is_negative), and is reported as such and never as a gain
honest_size: required of any 'better' reading, as the supervisor requires of M2h's: the gain is stated as a fraction of mean(D^2) over the held-out pairs beside the Delta MSE, so that a positive Delta MSE is read against the variance it is explaining and not alone
stop_rule: one run, from this registration's committed code, on the files the registration pins by sha256 (the 24 compiled programs, the rate table, the gene table, the narrowPeak files, this lane's census and the thirteen RNA quantifications). No form, parameter, population rule, split, scale definition, endpoint, pseudocount, metric, interval, control, decision, falsifier or wording is changed after a held-out value is read; a defect found afterwards is reported beside the registered reading and corrected only under a new registration
limitations: independence: each element's removal fold comes from AlphaGenome's RNA-seq gene scorer (an in-silico deletion, the argmax over 371 RNA-seq tracks), a model trained on ENCODE and GTEx RNA-seq, with RNA-seq tracks named for the reader biosamples among them, and on ENCODE DNase-seq; the reader's open/closed calls are ENCODE DNase-seq narrowPeak files of the same biosamples; the measured outcome is ENCODE polyA plus RNA-seq of those biosamples, data of the kind, and possibly the very experiments, the model was trained on. The cross-cell pattern of a gated prediction comes from the DNase calls alone and the size of each element's part from the model

the fit treats a gene's k observations as taken at one intact state, but each is the argmax over 371 tracks in its own track, and each reader cell's run transports them there. A maximum per element inflates each element's fold; under `or` that inflation raises q and so removes genes from the population rather than widening their predicted range

7d's POPULATION above is carried verbatim and its clause (d), 'the joint fit under F is runnable', is read with F = `or` and FIT['or']; clause (e)'s informativeness and clause (f)'s symbol and row checks are unchanged. The population is therefore NOT 7d's gene set: `or`'s q exceeds the mean's, so genes whose summed drops saturate it leave no positive basal rate and drop out, while `or` admits inhibitors the mean refuses and keeps genes 7d's mean does not run (FIT['q_rises_with_the_product']). The census counts the overlap, and the head-to-head is on the genes the compared forms both run

`or` is a form the engine carries and lane-combine compared against published cases on 2026-09-28; it is not a published model of these genes. Independent binding of any one of up to dozens of compiled elements, in thirteen cell types, is a declared form, not a measured mechanism

declared, not measured: the competition form's promoter occupancy THETA = 0.5 and one transcriptional efficiency per gene; the DECLARED_STRENGTH convention fixing the scale of s; the bridge's Hill assumptions (K = 1, n = 2, h = 0.5), which decide which inhibitors are feasible (s <= 1)

accessibility near a gene tracks its expression across cell types whatever any compiled rule says; an open element is one a rule may act through, not evidence that it does, and no reading here is evidence of a mechanism

one polyA plus experiment per biosample, from several labs; two of the thirteen are tissues (ovary, testis). Every rate under the run is mouse NIH 3T3 or their genome median; no fold prediction depends on it and no level in molecules per cell is quoted
descriptives: the uncalibrated held-out and whole-population Delta MSE at scale 1, beside the calibrated one
the head-to-heads against 7d's runtime mean and 7h's multiplicative composition over the genes both forms run, uncalibrated and at each form's own scale: descriptive, deciding nothing

a POST HOC 1-Mb locus-cluster bootstrap of the held-out Delta MSE beside the registered gene-level one, labelled post hoc, deciding nothing and never replacing the registered interval: genes sharing elements are not independent, which the supervisor's audit of M2h raised, and a cluster bootstrap resamples 1-Mb bins of the genome instead of genes

decisions: the arm: `or`, not `max`. The census (data/results/maxform_census.json, no RNA read) found `max`'s prediction differs from the runtime mean's on 0 of the 17,983 multi-element genes, because it fits only the 283 with ONE activating element -- where it IS the mean element for element -- and has no fit at all on the other 17,432 (maxform.PREMISE). That is NOT_TESTABLE under 7d's MIN_GENES and it is structural, not a small sample. `or` differs on 1,927 fitted genes, 1,843 of them informative with a symbol on exactly one gene_id, so it is the arm this registration judges

design: 7d's population and endpoint with lane-magcal's M2h analysis. POPULATION (a)-(c) and (f), the endpoint (ENCODE polyA plus RNA-seq of the thirteen reader biosamples, log2(TPM+1)), the no-rule baseline, the centring, MIN_GENES and the harness are combine2's, unchanged; (d) runnable and (e) informative are `or`'s. The scale fit, the held-out split, the metric, the within-gene cell permutation control, the four-way decision table and the outcome sentences are magcal's, imported and not reimplemented; no file of lane-magcal's is edited

the interval: 98.75%, percentiles 0.625 and 99.375, Bonferroni over a family of FOUR -- 7d's runtime mean, 7d's promoter competition, 7h's multiplicative composition and this arm. It is the same question, the same RNA and the same split as M2h's three arms, so a fourth arm changes the correction. Ruled by the supervisor through the coordinator on 2026-10-10 before any value was read. M2h's three readings keep their registered 98.33% intervals and are NOT recomputed

magcal's bootstrap_delta and bootstrap_scale read magcal's own FORM_INTERVAL, so this lane calls magcal's `_sums` and `_gene_terms` and applies its own percentile pair; tests/test_maxform.py checks that, run at magcal.FORM_INTERVAL, it reproduces magcal's two functions exactly

head-to-heads against the runtime mean and the multiplicative form are DESCRIPTIVE and decide nothing: this lane's registered endpoint is the calibrated held-out one, and the comparators are 7d's and 7h's committed rows, which M2h already calibrated. They are reported because the lane was asked for them, labelled as deciding nothing

the 1-Mb locus-cluster bootstrap is POST HOC, labelled as such, deciding nothing and never replacing the registered gene-level interval. It is computed because genes sharing elements are not independent, which the supervisor's audit of M2h raised

no root is picked anywhere: `or`'s fit is unique in closed form (maxform.FIT ['the_or_root_is_unique']), so lane-rootpick's registered root convention is cited and applies vacuously; `max` has no root at all on a gene with two or more activating elements

code_cleanliness.counting_path_is_computed: the transitive import closure of this script, computed from the files' import statements at write time (genomeos.manifest.counting_path), never by importing: it follows every import that resolves to a file in this repository rather than only the package, counts the __init__.py of each package above a module, resolves bare imports against the directories the source literally puts on sys.path as well as the repository root, and matches every path component against what its directory lists, so a class name such as genomeos.genome.Genome cannot enter it as a file; not a hand-written list
